overall: Violation found: the Monson Select Board's notice listing only "Code of Conduct" did not sufficiently describe its September 23 discussion of a specific incident. Individual-notice and town-policy/due-process claims were declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Sept. 23 meeting notice listing only "Code of Conduct" under New Business was insufficiently specific about the topic discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Under these facts, the topic “Code of Conduct,” did not sufficiently describe the anticipated discussion.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board should have given him individual notice that it would discuss him at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the discussion was held in open session, and not in executive session under Purpose 1, the Board was not required to give individual notice to the complainant or to any of the other individuals mentioned by name during the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board violated Town policy and due process in connection with the September 23 discussion.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not concern compliance with municipal policies or due process.

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
